title: Quarterly Engagement Slate — Standard & Enterprise Packs
content:
Purpose and intent:
This doc is a working slate of two compact QBR packs we can reuse across accounts: a Standard Pack for mid-market customers and an Enterprise Pack for strategic accounts. Goal is to make runbooks repeatable, reduce prep time, and give CSMs a consistent one-page narrative + appendix they can tailor in 30–60 minutes.

How to use this file:
- Pick Standard or Enterprise pack as the base.
- Fill in the metrics table (page 3) with O12W numbers and a short commentary.
- Highlight 1–2 success stories and 1–2 known risks.
- Use the ‘Ask & Next Steps’ slide to capture commitments and dates.

Audience and cadence considerations:
- Standard Pack: monthly or quarterly cadence; 30–45 minute meeting; CSM + Success Manager + Customer Ops counterpart. Use for accounts with predictable usage patterns and < $75k ARR.
- Enterprise Pack: quarterly executive + product alignment; 45–75 minute meeting; CSM, AM, Solutions Eng, and a customer exec sponsor. Use for accounts where renewal decision or expansion > $75k ARR is on the horizon.

Agenda templates (timed):
- Standard (30–45m)
  1) 5m — Executive snapshot (health score, NPS, top artifact)
  2) 10m — Usage & outcomes (what product delivered this period)
  3) 10m — Open items & blockers (inc. incident summary)
  4) 5–10m — Next steps & operational asks (owners + due dates)

- Enterprise (60–75m)
  1) 10m — Exec summary & strategic alignment (value realized vs. contract goals)
  2) 15m — Deep dive: performance, latency, cost per token (for Redwood users), and feature adoption
  3) 15m — Risks, mitigation plan, and fallback policies (capacity/region concerns)
  4) 15m — Roadmap alignment (product or infra items that affect the customer)
  5) 10–20m — Commercial discussion & next steps (renewal timeline, opportunities, formal asks)

Slide-by-slide outline (suggested speaker notes):
- Slide 1: Title + meeting context\  Speaker note: Name, role, timeframe covered, key objective of this meeting.

- Slide 2: One-line executive snapshot\  Speaker note: 3 bullets — value delivered, risk level (green/amber/red), one KPI trend line. Keep to under 30 seconds.

- Slide 3: Outcomes & usage highlights (Standard: 3 bullets; Enterprise: 4–6 bullets + chart)\  Speaker note: Tie bullets to business outcomes (time saved, revenue enabled, model accuracy improvements). If applicable, include a succinct example (customer workflow).

- Slide 4: Health metrics table (metrics below)\  Suggested metrics column headers: Metric | Current | Prior period | Target | Owner | Notes\  Metrics to include (choose 6): API requests/day, p50 latency (ms), p95 latency (ms), tokens per successful request, error rate %, cost/Tt (token throughput), adoption rate of new endpoints, eval regression count.

- Slide 5: Incidents & stability summary\  Speaker note: List incident dates, impact, RCA status, and whether follow-up action completed. Keep brief; link to runbook.

- Slide 6: Risk register (Top 3)\  Speaker note: For each risk include: trigger, mitigation, fallback plan (e.g., model variant, region reroute).

- Slide 7: Opportunities & roadmap alignment\  Speaker note: 1–3 items where customer can benefit (e.g., batching suggestions, quantization pilot, dedicated capacity conversation). Include estimated impact where possible.

- Slide 8: Commercial snapshot (Enterprise only)\  Speaker note: Contract end date, committed capacity, usage vs commit, forecast renewal posture (Green/At Risk/Red), proposed next steps. Avoid negotiation language in the deck; keep numbers factual.

- Slide 9: Ask & next steps (action register)\  Speaker note: Table of Owner | Action | Due date | Status. Call out any executive asks in bold.

- Appendix: Supporting artifacts (graphs, logs, eval diffs, PRs)\  Speaker note: Reference links to Confluence, Jira tickets, GH issues for technical follow-up.

One-page prep checklist for CSM (copy into the calendar invite):
- Pre-meeting: update metrics table (O12W).
- Pre-meeting: confirm exec attendees and alignment objective.
- Pre-meeting: gather one livable success story (customer quote or recorded metric).
- Pre-meeting: mark any open Sev tickets and status.
- Pre-meeting: draft 1–2 commercial asks with rationale.

Compact renewal / commitment tracker (to include in appendix or share separately):
Column headings (single-line friendly): Account | ARR band | Contract End | Current posture | Usage vs Commit | Primary Owner | Renewal ETA | Key blockers | Last CS Touch | Next Meeting
Notes on posture states: Active (green), Watch (amber), At Risk (red). Guidance: any account where usage < 60% of commit for 3 consecutive months -> mark Watch and add solutions eng review.

Template language: Executive opener (30–45s) — use plain language\"We partnered with your team to reduce inference cost and improve latency for live chat workflows. Over the last quarter we saw X% reduction in p95 latency and Y% increase in successful completions, which translates to fewer escalations and faster time-to-first-response for your agents. Today we want to align on operational improvements and the few items that could block next-quarter scale.\"

Risk communication guidance (tone & structure):
- Start with impact (what went down and who felt it).
- Provide root cause summary in one sentence.
- State the mitigation and the expected timing.
- If an executive-level ask is needed, put it in the ‘Ask’ slide and label it ‘Exec decision required’.

Example tailored asks (short):
- Operational ask: Increase max tokens per request to 8k for the triage pipeline; impact: ~15% fewer round trips. Owner: Platform Eng.
- Commercial ask: Consider moving from shared-hosted to dedicated pool to stabilize latency during peak hours. Owner: AM.

Post-meeting follow-up template (email):
Subject: QBR recap — [Account] — [Quarter]
Hi [Name],
Thanks for taking the time today. Attached is the brief we covered; below are the agreed next steps.
1) [Owner] — [Action] — [Due date]
2) [Owner] — [Action] — [Due date]
Open items we committed to follow-up on: [short bullets].
If you have edits to the notes or want a follow-up on X, reply and we’ll schedule.
Best,
[CSM name]

Operational tips & reuse patterns (CSM hints):
- Keep the first two slides intentionally short and visual. Execs want 60s of signal.
- Use green/amber/red consistently across slides and in the action register.
- For Enterprise packs always include a short cost vs. value slide (what we saved vs. what we charge next period).
- Archive the meeting pack to Confluence with a copy of the appendix artifacts and link to the Jira(s).

Open questions / TODOs for the team:
- Finalize the health metric definitions (p50 vs p95 naming) — owner: Jonas.
- Add a templated visual for cost per thousand tokens (owner: Priya).
- Create a one-click sheet that populates the metrics table from our analytics export (engineer ticket CS-4123).

Appendix: Quick copy-paste snippets
- Exec summary one-liner: [Customer] saw a [X%] improvement in p95 latency and [Y%] reduction in cost per successful request over the last quarter.
- Risk flag short: [Issue] — impact [high|medium|low] — mitigation [short].
